Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1248 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
THE NORTHEAST...FROM CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA INTO NORTHWEST
NEBRASKA...AND FROM SOUTHERN KANSAS INTO NORTHWEST OKLAHOMA...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur over small parts of the Great Plains,
and over the Northeast on Thursday with locally strong wind gusts.
Isolated hail may occur with the Northern Plains activity.

...Central SD into northwest NE...
A shortwave trough will move southeastward across SK/MB, with at
least some influence extending southward across the northern Plains.
A surface trough will develop southward into central SD and western
NE, where strong heating will occur. A narrow band of uncapped
instability is forecast, with several models indicating scattered
storms late in the day. Southerly 850 mb winds over 20 kt will
aid/maintain moisture into the area, and forecast soundings show
marginally favorable hodographs for supercells. Localized hail may
occur initially, with some clustering and wind potential into the
early evening.

...Southern KS into northwest OK...
A surface trough/wind shift is forecast to exist from southern KS
into northern OK, with southerly winds and strong heating to the
south. Near/north of the boundary, winds will remain southeasterly
with higher dewpoints. General model consensus is for the deeply
mixed boundary layer to support an uncapped air mass, with a zone of
storms developing. These will likely produce strong outflow, and a
few severe gusts may occur.

...Northeast...
Southwest winds aloft will persist over the region as an upper high
remains over the Atlantic and a shortwave trough approaches the
Lower Great Lakes by late afternoon. Height tendencies will remain
neutral from NY into WV/VA during the day, but strong heating, PWAT
near 2.00" and sufficient MUCAPE should aid scattered storm
development near a weak surface trough after 19Z. This would include
from south-central NY into central PA and across the higher terrain
of western VA. A few strong gusts cannot be ruled out.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0229 PM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
MID-ATLANTIC...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur from the central Plains into the
Northeast on Thursday with locally strong wind gusts.

...Northeast...
A very moist airmass (dewpoints in the low/mid 70s F) are expected
across much of the East along the western periphery of the Atlantic
surface high. Flow aloft will be somewhat enhanced near the Great
Lakes trough, primarily for the northern Mid-Atlantic into parts of
New England. Given the rich moisture, surface heating will not have
to be overly robust to promote around or above 2000 J/kg MLCAPE
despite weak mid-level lapse rates. Where steeper low-level lapse
rates and/or clustering can occur, isolated damaging winds will be
possible.

...Central/Northern Plains...
Predictability continues to be low within these regions. In southern
Kansas, the cold font, perhaps augmented by early day
precipitation/clouds, will be one area of potential storm
development during the afternoon. Temperatures to the south of the
stalled boundary will be quite hot and may provide enough lift for
initiation. Enough mid-level flow will be present to promote storm
organization, should any form. Uncertainty in development remains
too high for a categorical risk area.

A secondary surface front is expected to develop from northern
Nebraska into the eastern Dakotas and northern Minnesota. The ECMWF
is much more aggressive with moisture return ahead of the boundary
than the NAM. Furthermore, mid-level heights will likely be slowly
rising through the period. A stronger storm or two would be
possible, but development is still uncertain. Elevated storms are
probable in northern Minnesota as the low-level jet increases, but
buoyancy is expected to remain weak.

..Wendt.. 08/04/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0400 AM CDT Tue Aug 04 2026

Valid 071200Z - 121200Z

...DISCUSSION...
An upper high will remain over the southwestern states through much
of the period, with a deep upper low gradually shifting eastward
across Ontario Canada. In between, a zone of moderate northwest flow
aloft will exist from the northern Plains/Upper MS Valley across the
Great Lakes. At the surface, low pressure will exist over the
central High Plains, with an east-west boundary roughly along I-80
from Nebraska eastward.

Stronger cyclonic flow aloft will move out of the northern Plains on
Fri/D4 and increase across the Great Lakes and into the Northeast
from Sat/D5 through the end of the period, with midlevel winds
around 30-40 kt possibly overspreading the surface front. A large
area of upper 60s to lower 70s F dewpoints will remain along and
south of the boundary, which may shift north/south as disturbances
rotate around the Canadian upper low. Predictability remains low for
denoting precise MCS corridors, but timing of the upper wave
amplifications will be monitored in subsequent forecast cycles, with
possible risk areas mainly for damaging wind potential.

..Jewell.. 08/04/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1231 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS...AND SOUTHEASTERN
ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and hail will be
possible from this afternoon into the overnight across parts of the
mid Mississippi Valley. Isolated severe gusts may also occur in
parts of the southern High Plains, and in southeastern Arizona.

...Mid Mississippi Valley...
An upper-level trough will move eastward today across the
north-central U.S. At the surface, a quasi-stationary front will be
located from the central Plains northeastward into the mid
Mississippi Valley. Along and to the south of the front, surface
dewpoints will be in the lower to mid 70s F. As surface temperatures
warm today, moderate instability will develop to the south of the
front. Large-scale ascent associated with the trough will support
scattered to numerous thunderstorm development from this afternoon
into tonight across much of Missouri and Illinois. 

RAP forecast soundings late this afternoon near the instability axis
in northeast Missouri have MLCAPE near 2000 j/kg, with 0-6 km shear
around 35 knots. This may support supercell development with storms
that remain discrete. However, high-resolution models suggest that
storm mode could be more favorable for multicells due to widespread
convective coverage. Although low-level lapse rates will be poor,
the instability and moderate deep-layer shear could be enough for
isolated severe wind gusts and hail.

...Southern High Plains...
West-northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place today across much
of the central U.S. A small pocket of moderate instability is
forecast to develop over southeast Colorado this afternoon. This
will aid convective initiation in the foothills of the southern
Rockies. During the late afternoon and early evening, storms are
expected to move east-southeastward into the lower elevations of the
northwestern Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma Panhandle. The
instability and steep low to mid-level lapse rates may support an
isolated threat for severe wind gusts.

...Southeastern Arizona...
A sufficiently moist airmass will be in place today across southern
Arizona. As surface temperatures warm, moderate instability will
develop over much of southeast Arizona by afternoon. Convection is
expected to form in the higher terrain of southwest New Mexico, with
storms moving west-southwestward across southeast Arizona from late
afternoon into the early evening. Very steep low-level lapse rates
and large temperature-dewpoint spreads will contribute to a
potential for isolated severe wind gusts.

..Broyles/Supinie.. 08/05/2026
